title: Chinese robot dancers find rhythm on American talent show
key_facts: Chinese dancer Wu Yufei, 27, from Sichuan province, performed at the America's Got Talent finale with humanoid robots made by Unitree.
The act mixed robotics, inkwash aesthetics and contemporary stage performance, and was directed by Chengdu choreographer Fang Zhenghua.
At the audition the robots danced and flipped in time with the music and all four judges voted yes.
By the 8 Sep quarterfinals the act was doing martial arts with human dancers.
Judge Howie Mandel predicted it would be "the most viral moment we're going to have this season".
Actress Sofia Vergara pressed the Golden Buzzer, sending the team directly to the 22 Sep final.
The article does not say how the act placed in the final.
quote_evidence: At the finale, the 27-year-old from Sichuan province in southwestern China shared the stage with humanoid robots made by Unitree, performing in a fusion of robotics, inkwash aesthetics and contemporary stage performance.
Judge Howie Mandel imagined a martial arts version of the Will Smith film I, Robot and predicted it would be "the most viral moment we're going to have this season".
Actress Sofia Vergara pressed the Golden Buzzer, sending the team directly to the Sept 22 final.
why_it_matters_hint: Humanoid robots are being used as stage performers on a major US TV show, shown in a feature by Chinese state media.
event_date: Final on 22 Sep 2026; article published 17 Oct 2026
notes: China Daily is a Chinese state-run paper; this is a feature on events that happened weeks earlier (quarterfinal 8 Sep, final 22 Sep 2026), so the entry is stale. The article does not give the final result.
